Author: K. Lakshman
Bench: K. Lakshman
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman
 Writ Petition No.14109 Of 2024
Oral Order

: 
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 3 and also Mr. L. Prabhakar Reddy, learned Standing Counsel for TSIIC appearing on behalf of respondent No.4.
2.
According to the petitioners, they are in possession of the lands admeasuring Acs.3.20 guntas each in Survey No.300/25, 300/24 and 300/23 and they are cultivating by raising crops.
Originally their ancestors were granted assignment by the Government and their names were also mutated in revenue records.
Being the legal heirs of their ancestors, they are in possession of the subject lands and it is only source of their livelihood.
Even then, respondent Nos.3 and 4 are trying to dispossess them without following due procedure laid down under law and without paying compensation.

3. Whereas, Mr. L. Prabhakar Reddy, learned Standing Counsel for respondent No.4, on instructions, would submit that the respondents have acquired the land admeasuring Acs.403.00 guntas in the aforesaid survey numbers and other survey numbers of Kongara Kalan Village for the purpose of establishing a 'Rice-hub' by following due procedure laid down under law.

4. If the subject property is required for any public purpose, respondent Nos.2 and 3 have to follow the due procedure laid down under law including the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

opennyai_summary.facts: Even then, respondent Nos.3 and 4 are trying to dispossess them without following due procedure laid down under law and without paying compensation.
opennyai_summary.arguments: 3. Whereas, Mr. L. Prabhakar Reddy, learned Standing Counsel for respondent No.4, on instructions, would submit that the respondents have acquired the land admeasuring Acs.403.00 guntas in the aforesaid survey numbers and other survey numbers of Kongara Kalan Village for the purpose of establishing a 'Rice-hub' by following due procedure laid down under law.
opennyai_summary.decision:
4. If the subject property is required for any public purpose, respondent Nos.2 and 3 have to follow the due procedure laid down under law including the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
They cannot dispossess the petitioners without following due procedure laid down under law.
5. In the light of the aforesaid submissions, this writ petition is disposed of directing respondent Nos.3 and 4 not to dispossess the petitioners from the subject lands without following the due procedure laid down under law including the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
If the subject land is required for any public purpose including establishment of rice-hub, liberty is granted to the respondents to take steps in accordance with law.
In the circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the writ petition shall stand closed.
